realFeedback: User corrected the ZX85 production model: the cabin is the parent physical assembly; roof, side walls, door, floor, operator console and seat are cabin children; joysticks, pedals, instruments, throttle and hydraulic lock are console children; engine and hydraulics remain separate whole-machine systems connected by typed control relations.
failurePrevented: flattening a parent assembly into an unowned list of individually impressive parts
claiming the cabin complete because a door, window, seat or control subassembly passed independently
attaching a child to the whole machine while bypassing its user-defined parent assembly
inventing control relationships or treating a placeholder relation as implemented simulation
using object, triangle, document or screenshot counts as proof of assembly progress
auditRules: every user-named physical system must have one stable objectId, one explicit parentObjectId and one installation coordinate frame
a child PASS never promotes its parent assembly; the parent remains incomplete while any required child, mounting relation or integration binding is missing
physical ownership and functional control relations are separate graphs and must not be collapsed
cross-system control relations must name source, target, semantics and implementation state; placeholders remain UNKNOWN or UNIMPLEMENTED
a child may be independently auditioned, but production replacement is forbidden until it is bound through the declared parent assembly
object, triangle, file, branch, document and screenshot counts are inventory only, never acceptance evidence

a whole-machine graph must consume the same assembly ownership contract; a standalone JSON tree without current integration binding is POSTED or GATE-RUN evidence, not IMPLEMENTED production structure
